title: Wes Kussmaul / Grace Rachmany / Josh Stein call, 2026-10-15: DIF, Creator Assertions WG, Osmio certification, technical vs political adoption crux

nodes.text: The ecovillage identity network is decentralized, not federated, because there is no single authority — there are multiple registries.
nodes.span: It's not federated because there isn't a single authority. There are multiple registries.

nodes.text: All ecovillages recognize each other, but the car-sharing fleet recognizes only 50 of them plus 20 non-ecovillage organizations — a different registry.
nodes.span: the fleet only recognizes 50 of them. Plus they recognize 20 other organizations that aren't ecovillages. So it's a different registry.

nodes.text: There is not one federation but two overlapping ones, like a Venn diagram.
nodes.span: There's two federations. There's some overlap. There's like a Venn diagram.

nodes.text: DIF, being a standards body rather than a company, has little to offer Osmio.
nodes.span: DIF isn't a company, DIF is a standards body and so I don't think we have a lot to offer you.

nodes.text: Without using DIDs, most DIF working groups won't be interesting to Osmio.
nodes.span: If you're not using DIDs, then most of our working groups aren't gonna be very interesting to you

nodes.text: Osmio already has a developed, working technology, so it is unclear why it would come to DIF.
nodes.span: It sounds like you've got a technology that you've developed that works. Why would you come to DIF?

nodes.text: Osmio's work is appropriate for DIF's Creator Assertions Working Group, which also supports X.509.
nodes.span: What you're talking about is really appropriate for the Creator Assertions Working Group

nodes.text: A working group founded by Adobe and the big players, two years in, will not listen to a newcomer like Osmio.
nodes.span: If you come into a working group that is founded by Adobe and all the big guys, they're not gonna listen to you. They've been working on this for two years.

nodes.text: Standards are typically not industry collaborations but the big players forcing their will (OpenID Foundation, Agentic AI Foundation).
nodes.span: They're not really industry collaborations. They're the big guys forcing their will.

nodes.text: Osmio is not big enough to force a standard on others, but big enough to run its own franchise its own way.
nodes.span: You're not big enough to stuff it down somebody's throat. You're big enough to have your own franchise of doing things the way you want.

nodes.text: Osmio is a unified-vision organization — effectively a franchising business, not a collaborative-vision body.
nodes.span: We are a unified vision organization. We're effectively a franchising business.

nodes.text: When vision comes from one source (Python, Apple, Drupal), interfaces between elements get developed faster and more effectively.
nodes.span: the vision comes from one collection of brain cells and that's why interfaces between elements tend to be more quickly developed and more effectively developed in organizations that are unified

nodes.text: Identity reliability is not binary; different uses need different reliability levels, as in NIST 800-63.
nodes.span: Identity reliability is not binary.

nodes.text: Osmio's assertion support certificate lets a relying party see an identity reliability score behind an identity claim.
nodes.span: the relying party can see the identity reliability score associated with that identity claim

nodes.text: Preventing Nazi-style misuse of identity databases is a technical question, solved by Osmio's Internet of People protocol: an identity database with no identity information in it.
nodes.span: We have the Internet of People protocol, which means we have an identity database with no identity information in it.

nodes.text: The historical threat of government identity databases (Germany, Netherlands) is amplified now that databases are online.
nodes.span: Now we have online databases and the threat is amplified.

nodes.text: The identity-database question is now a political question, not a technical one.
nodes.span: That question is a political question now. It's not a technical question.

nodes.text: Signing up for Osmio's identity does no practical good because one is forced into government ID for banking, healthcare and driver's licenses.
nodes.span: I can sign up for your identity. It won't do me a damn bit of good because I have zero choice if I wanna get healthcare.

nodes.text: Few can extract themselves from the existing system because no full alternative system is offered; you have to offer all the services.
nodes.span: Very few people are able to extract themselves from the existing system because you're not offering an alternative system. You have to offer all of the services.

nodes.text: Many people are ignoring banks these days.
nodes.span: A lot of people are ignoring banks these days.

nodes.text: After seven years in crypto, Grace knows very few people, even in the crypto industry, without a bank account.
nodes.span: I know very few people for whom it's their primary means, within the crypto industry, who don't have a bank account.

nodes.text: The identifier is only part of the system; that is why Grace starts with ecovillages and food systems.
nodes.span: The identifier is only part of the system. That's why I wanna work with ecovillages, because they have food.

nodes.text: Banks are threatened: KYC/KYCC are cracking, synthetic identities are rampant and will vanish in a downturn, causing serious problems for banking.
nodes.span: KYC and KYCC are cracking at the seams. Synthetic identities are rampant.

nodes.text: Grace agrees with the critique of banks but maintains the issue is adoption and what services an individual can get with the identity.
nodes.span: I agree with you on all of these things. What I'm saying is that this is an issue of adoption and of what service an individual can get with this identity.

nodes.text: Osmio's adoption answer is franchisees that target a painful problem in a specific audience (Deep Authenticity, HireEvo, Trusted and True).
nodes.span: That's why our franchisees focus on a particular problem in a particular audience that's painful.

nodes.text: Grace likes the franchise approach and thinks both are trying to do the same thing, with different adoption strategies.
nodes.span: I love that. I think we're trying to do the same thing. Your approach to adoption is really different from my approach to adoption.

nodes.text: For the ecovillage work, many technical solutions already meet the bar; it is not a technical problem at all.
nodes.span: there are many technical solutions which pass the standard that I would want. Many. It's not a technical problem at all.

nodes.text: The technical problems in identity are mostly resolved; the need is deployment in the world.
nodes.span: the technical problems are mostly resolved

nodes.text: Deployment is the reality — where the rubber meets the road.
nodes.span: Deployment is the reality. That's where the rubber meets the road.

nodes.text: Conversations like this are valuable for identifying what is known, what is argued for, and where disagreements and cruxes lie.
nodes.span: Even identifying where disagreements or gaps exist is valuable. It's valuable to see where you come to a crux.

nodes.text: There should be global infrastructure — perhaps a decentralized protocol or standard — providing a public record of debate.
nodes.span: create global infrastructure where these conversations can be useful and provide a public record of debate

nodes.text: The Talmud was an early on-paper protocol for recording communal debate, consensus and branching.
nodes.span: The Talmud was an early on-paper version of a protocol for recording communal debate

nodes.text: Regardless of disagreement on X.509, some layer exists that is global.
nodes.span: Whether or not we agree or disagree on X.509, there's still some layer that exists that is global regardless.

nodes.text: Global layers are a very modern idea and few things actually constitute global layers.
nodes.span: The idea of global layers is a very modern idea. And there isn't that much that makes up global layers.

nodes.text: Passports were interoperable long before NFC chips, without a standard — standards aren't always needed for interoperability.
nodes.span: long before there were NFC chips in them, they were interoperable

nodes.text: It is unclear why some things become standards (Bluetooth, USB-C) and others (video protocols) do not.
nodes.span: Why are some things a standard and some things aren't? I have no idea.

nodes.text: There is one space where a standard is required: knowing whether an online representation is a real person and whether they are who they claim to be.
nodes.span: there's one space where the answer is there must be a standard. We need to know whether the representation of a person online is A, really a person, not a bot, and B, are they who they claim to be?

nodes.text: There is more than one way to verify personhood, which is why people aren't coming to DIF — every member built its own standard.
nodes.span: Is there only one way to do that? No. That's why people aren't coming to DIF, because every one of our members has developed their own standard for that.

nodes.text: Without a central authority, an identity system can be corrupted.
nodes.span: If there's no central authority, then it can be corrupted.

nodes.text: A central authority can also be corrupted, and existing central authorities are failing badly — that is the worst possible world.
nodes.span: If there's a central authority, it can be corrupted. What's happening to all of our central authorities? It's really bad.

nodes.text: Osmio invites outside engineers and pen testers to try to corrupt its certification.
nodes.span: We're inviting you to bring your best engineers, your best pen testers to corrupt our certification.

nodes.text: Grace is absolutely opposed to one central authority that knows who all the people in the world are.
nodes.span: Absolutely opposed to one central authority that knows who all the people in the world are.

nodes.text: Osmio's certification holds no identity information, so the central-authority objection does not apply; examine it closely.
nodes.span: It doesn't have any identity information in it. Put it under the microscope.

nodes.text: A single central system doesn't work; it is too fragile — Grace does not believe in 'one world computer'.
nodes.span: I just think it doesn't work. It's too fragile.

nodes.text: PKCS/PKI standards have been hammered on for decades and hold up.
nodes.span: PKCS has been hammered on for decades and it holds up.

nodes.text: Even DNS has to be federated with multiple layers, because one system doesn't work.
nodes.span: Even the DNS system has to be federated in some way and it has multiple layers of how it works, because one system doesn't work.

nodes.text: Everyone touching DNS should be professionally licensed via Osmio's utility certificate and thus legally accountable.
nodes.span: Everyone in the DNS system should be professionally licensed to touch the DNS system, thus legally accountable for what they do.

nodes.text: Nobody is even close to such a licensed/global system; the closest existing thing is Aadhaar.
nodes.span: none of us are even mildly close to that. The closest you've got is the Aadhaar system.

nodes.text: Wes agrees Aadhaar is horrible, which is why Osmio has a group working on a global stack.
nodes.span: Oh, Aadhaar is horrible.

nodes.text: Global identity is a practical question; like Network School and Liberland, Osmio is a normal, not bad, idea — but right now it is only an idea.
nodes.span: It's not a bad idea, but right now it's an idea.

nodes.text: Osmio is already developed and being deployed, not merely an idea; Grace hasn't looked into it.
nodes.span: Right now, it's developed; it's being deployed.

nodes.text: Osmio is a municipality that grew out of and continues the ITU.
nodes.span: It's a municipality. It grew out of, it's the continuation of the ITU.

nodes.text: C2PA handles content provenance (whether a camera took the content) but deliberately avoids identity — what camera, whose camera.
nodes.span: C2PA didn't want to touch identity. They can say a camera took this, but they don't want to say what camera, whose camera.

nodes.text: The Creator Assertions Working Group addresses how to attach identity assertions to a C2PA manifest.
nodes.span: If there's something called a C2PA manifest, how do we stick some identity assertions on that?

nodes.text: The Creator Assertions group will be quite centralized because of the kind of large entities involved.
nodes.span: It's gonna be quite centralized because that's the kind of entities they are.

nodes.text: A photo can be digitally signed by both the photographer and the camera.
nodes.span: A photo can be digitally signed by the photographer and by the camera.
